subject: botany
question_text: How are the petals in the pea plant arranged? What is such a type of arrangement called?

verification.note: Chapter 5 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany book (pp.9-14), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO asked-year citations, so the missing stars/appearances record an absence of signal, not zero frequency. insider_note: Papilionaceous corolla AND vexillary aestivation - the second term is the one that separates full marks from half.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The five petals
lines: The pea flower has five unequal petals:
overlaps the two lateral wings (alae), and
the wings overlap the two smallest anterior
steps.why: The scoring facts are the counts and the overlap order: 1 standard over 2 wings over 2 keel petals - large to small, back to front.
common_mistakes: Writing five equal petals. The corolla is unequal - that is the point of the question.
Reversing the overlap - the standard is outermost, the keel innermost.
steps.memory_tip: 1 standard, 2 wings, 2 keel - 1+2+2 = 5, each layer covering the next.
steps.margin_note: Give the three technical names with their common names in brackets.

steps.label: Name of the arrangement

lines.text: Such a corolla is called papilionaceous;

steps.why: Two names close the answer: papilionaceous for the corolla type, vexillary for its aestivation - both are asked by 'what is it called'.
common_mistakes: Giving only papilionaceous. Vexillary aestivation is the second half of the naming.
steps.memory_tip: Vexillum leads, so the aestivation is vexillary; the whole corolla is papilionaceous.
steps.margin_note: Both terms in one boxed line - this is the mark most students drop.
